findings.element: PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", …) — _gate-suite.html:20190-20192, `C.rootEl()` inside the IIFE that spans _gate-suite.html:20040-20319, where `C` is never declared (`var C = window.__TLCORE` is at _gate-suite.html:20345, inside the NEXT IIFE)
findings.problem: Every crossing of the 720px phone query throws `Uncaught ReferenceError: C is not defined` at _gate-suite.html:20191, in all three products (reproduced by resizing tasks.board, notes.notebook and timeline.owner-flight from 1440 to 720 — one throw each, in both directions). The handler's whole job is to re-render the timeline for the new layout, so it does nothing at all. The consequence is measured: timeline.owner-flight loaded fresh at 390 gives data-layout="down", zero layout toggles and the action bar folded to "Add a moment · ···". The SAME state narrowed from 1440 to 390 gives data-layout="across", TWO visible [data-layout-to] buttons and the full desk bar "Add a moment / Preview / Get the link" — so the phone gets the across composition and the layout toggle that the 2 September ledger decided is never offered on a phone, plus a three-button desk bar at 390. Enlarging back does not repair it either; the state is stuck at whatever the first paint chose. The behaviour gate cannot see this: it opens each state fresh at a fixed viewport and never resizes, and document overflow stays 0 so the sideways-scroll assertions stay green. A person rotating a phone, a tablet entering split view, or anyone dragging a browser window narrower gets this surface.
findings.fix: Two lines. In the IIFE at _gate-suite.html:20040, add `var C = window.__TLCORE;` beside the other module handles at the top of that IIFE (or replace the reference at :20191 with `window.__TLCORE.rootEl()`), so the handler runs instead of throwing. Then, because the handler currently re-renders only when the state is owner-flight, widen it to re-render whatever is mounted: `PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", function () { var st = window.__TLCORE.rootEl().getAttribute("data-state"); if (st) go(st); });`. Add to interaction-check.mjs a resize assertion for every state and every crossing: open at 1440, setViewportSize to 390 and back, and require (a) pageErrors unchanged, and (b) that the post-resize DOM matches a fresh load at that width on data-layout, the count of visible [data-layout-to], and the visible .b-act labels.

findings.element: [data-act="open-task"].deskFactLink → openTask() at _gate-suite.html:11007-11019, against Notes' offerUndo/doUndo at _gate-suite.html:16137-16200 and the three per-product Ctrl+Z handlers at _gate-suite.html:14197 (tasks), :19509 (notes), :22171-22190 (timeline), each guarded on window.__SUITE.active(<product>)
findings.problem: Driven at 1440 on notes.seam, the suite's own primary journey: press Send to Tasks ("Sent to Tasks. Your note stayed here. In The house.", card seam_n14_1 lands in To do, the strip reads "Undo · Ctrl Z · for 30 seconds"). The seam hands focus to "Open in Tasks"; press Enter; you arrive in Tasks with focus on the card that just landed. Press Ctrl+Z — the binding the strip you were reading a second ago advertised — and the suite answers "Nothing left to undo." while the seam's 30-second window is still counting down and the card is still under your hand. Nothing is undone. Arriving via the rail behaves the same. Walk back to Notes and the identical keystroke works ("Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks.") and removes the card from both products. There are three independent undo stacks, each answering only for its own product, so the ONE act that by definition crosses products is the one act whose reversal the surface actively denies. "Nothing left to undo." is not a missing feature here; it is a false statement about the suite's state, spoken into the live region at the moment a person is least sure, on the gesture the whole suite exists to argue for.
findings.fix: Give the router one cross-product receipt. In the suite IIFE add `var crossAct = null;` and expose `__SUITE.armCross = function (act) { crossAct = act; }` and `__SUITE.takeCross = function () { var a = crossAct; if (!a || Date.now() > a.until) { crossAct = null; return null; } crossAct = null; return a; }`. In Notes' offerUndo (_gate-suite.html:16137), when the label is the seam's ("Sent to Tasks."), also call `window.__SUITE.armCross({ until: Date.now() + UNDO_SECONDS * 1000, undoneLabel: undoneLabel, run: function () { doUndo(); } })`, and clear it in the expiry timeout at :16159. Then in each of the three Ctrl+Z handlers, replace the bare `say("Nothing left to undo.")` with `const cross = window.__SUITE.takeCross(); if (cross) { cross.run(); window.__SUITE.say(cross.undoneLabel); return; } say("Nothing left to undo.");` — Notes' doUndo already reverts both sides, so no new revert logic is needed. Also carry the receipt with the person: in openTask() (_gate-suite.html:11014) render the same strip in the arriving product's undo home while the window is live, so the way back is visible and not only bound to a key. Add to interaction-check.mjs: send from notes.seam, press Open in Tasks, press Ctrl+Z, and require the card gone from the board and the sentence to say the note was taken back.

findings.element: `let view = matchMedia("(max-width: 1099px)").matches ? "list" : "board";` — _gate-suite.html:11496, read once at script parse and never given a `change` listener (compare the 720 query at _gate-suite.html:11507-11509, which does get one)
findings.problem: The board/list rule is evaluated exactly once, at load. tasks.board loaded fresh at 390 correctly opens the List (segmented control reads "Board, List*", zero lanes rendered, board scrollWidth 372 = clientWidth). The same state narrowed from 1440 to 390 stays on the Board: five lanes visible and a board whose scrollWidth is 1520px inside a 372px viewport — a five-lane kanban paging sideways on a phone, which is the surface the 2 September ledger decided against ("below 1100 the board is a LIST"). It never repairs: enlarging and re-narrowing leaves it wherever the first paint put it. Document overflow stays 0 because the board is its own scroller, so every sideways-scroll assertion stays green, and the gate never resizes, so 129 assertions cannot see it.
findings.fix: Promote the query to a live one, matching what the 720 query already does. Replace the one-shot read with `const LIST_Q = matchMedia("(max-width: 1099px)"); let view = LIST_Q.matches ? "list" : "board"; let viewChosen = false;` — set `viewChosen = true` in the segmented control's handler at _gate-suite.html:14575 so an explicit human choice is never overridden — then `LIST_Q.addEventListener("change", (e) => { if (viewChosen) return; const next = e.matches ? "list" : "board"; if (next === view) return; view = next; mount(); });`. mount() already restores scroll and focus, so no place-keeping work is needed. Cover it in interaction-check.mjs with the same fresh-vs-resized comparison the crossing finding asks for: at 390 require the List selected and zero .tray sections rendered whether the width was arrived at by loading or by resizing.

findings.element: .card[data-id] Space-to-drop branch of onKey() — _gate-suite.html:14304-14324 (compare the pointer drop at _gate-suite.html:15114 and the move menu at _gate-suite.html:14887, which both call arm({kind:"move"}))
findings.problem: Driven at 1440 on tasks.board: focus a card, Space ("Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company."), ArrowRight ArrowRight, Space. The board says "...dropped in the review column." Ctrl+Z then answers "Nothing left to undo." and the card stays in Review. The identical move by mouse drag answers "...is back in the to do column.", and the same move through the card's Move menu is undoable too. Only the keyboard-carry drop fails to arm, because the Space branch of onKey mutates the lane and never calls arm(). Escape covers the card only while it is still in hand; once Space commits, the keyboard route is the one route to the board's most frequent structural act with no way back. The card advertises aria-roledescription="Movable task" and aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight", so this is precisely the promise the surface makes to the operator who cannot drag. A keyboard drop into Done IS undoable, because completed() arms — which is why the gap survives anyone who only tests the completion.
findings.fix: In the Space-to-drop branch of onKey, before the mutation read `const heldWas = task.heldSince, doneWas = task.completedAt;`, then in the non-Done branch replace the bare `say(task.title + " dropped " + inLane(lane) + ".")` with `arm({ kind: "move", id: id, title: task.title, lane: carriedFrom.lane, index: carriedFrom.index, toLane: lane, wasHeldSince: heldWas, wasCompletedAt: doneWas }); say(task.title + " dropped " + inLane(lane) + ". Press " + keycap("Z") + " to undo.");` — runUndo's default branch already restores lane, index, heldSince and completedAt, so no new undo kind is needed. Add to interaction-check.mjs: carry a card two lanes by keyboard, drop with Space, press Ctrl+Z, require the card back in its original lane and the sentence to say so.
